calculation_handling.description: If front-yard averaging (10.5.40.70(1)) does not apply, the minimum front yard setback in the R zone is 6.0 metres.
The minimum rear yard setback in the R zone is 7.5 metres.

Minimum side yard setback of 0.9 metres for a detached house, semi-detached house, detached houseplex, semi-detached houseplex, a townhouse whose units all front directly on a street, and an apartment building 13.0 metres or less in height.
calculation_handling.gaps: The two qualifiers are type-specific (all_units_front_street only for townhouse; height 13.0 m or less only for apartment building) and cannot be keyed as a unit-wide conjunctive condition, so condition is none and the 13.0 m threshold is listed as not expressed. Item (v) was deleted by By-law 648-2025.

calculation_handling.description: Minimum side yard setback of 7.5 metres for a townhouse where a dwelling unit does not front directly on a street, an apartment building more than 13.0 metres in height, and a non-residential building.
calculation_handling.gaps: Type-specific qualifiers (townhouse with a unit not fronting a street; apartment over 13.0 m) cannot be keyed as a unit-wide condition; the negated all_units_front_street token is not expressible.

calculation_handling.description: For a detached house, the side yard setback in 10.10.40.70(3) may be reduced to 0.45 metres on a side with no windows or doors.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to a side of the building with no windows or doors, a design input with no vocab token; keyed as a reduced minimum.

units.disclosure: The side setback can drop to 0.45 m only on a wall with no windows or doors; we do not know your wall design.

calculation_handling.description: Despite (1)-(4), a townhouse or apartment building on a lot abutting a major street has a minimum front yard setback: on a lot 36.0 m deep or less, the lesser of the front-yard averaging setback (10.5.40.70(1)) or 6.0 m where averaging applies, 3.0 m where it does not, and 6.0 m on a through lot; on a lot deeper than 36.0 m, 6.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The expression captures only the (i)(b) 3.0 m arm and the (ii) 6.0 m arm. Arm (i)(a) (lesser of the averaging setback or 6.0 m) needs the averaging result, which is not a DSL variable, and arm (i)(c) (6.0 m on a through lot) needs a token test the grammar has no atom for. On a shallow lot where averaging applies or on a through lot the result may be wrong.

units.disclosure: On major-street lots the front setback for townhouses and apartments depends on front-yard averaging and through-lot status, which we only partly evaluate.

calculation_handling.description: A townhouse or apartment building on a lot abutting a major street has a minimum rear yard setback of 7.5 metres.
A townhouse on a lot abutting a major street has a minimum side yard setback of 0.9 m if all dwelling units front directly onto a street, otherwise 7.5 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The two arms are selected by the all_units_front_street token, which the condition grammar cannot test inside an expression; both statements are listed by arm. Evaluated together the stricter 7.5 m would govern, so the result is conservative unless the user confirms all units front the street.

units.disclosure: A townhouse on a major street needs 0.9 m side yards if every unit faces the street, otherwise 7.5 m; tell us your layout.

calculation_handling.description: An apartment building on a lot abutting a major street has minimum side yard setbacks of 1.8 m for main-wall portions without primary windows, 5.5 m for portions with primary windows, 7.5 m for portions beyond a building length of 25.0 m, and on a corner lot 3.0 m from a side lot line abutting a street.
calculation_handling.gaps: Wall-portion-specific arms (windows / length beyond 25.0 m) cannot be selected from lot data; the 25.0 m length threshold is portion-based and not expressed. Arm (iv) is a different target (side_setback_street_m) and applies only on a corner_lot, which the unit-wide condition cannot scope to that statement. Apartment buildings are outside the core MaxBLD types.

units.disclosure: Apartment side setbacks on major streets vary by wall portion (windows, length) and corner-lot status; only partly evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite (D), an apartment building on a through lot abutting a major street has minimum side yard setbacks of 2.4 m for main-wall portions without primary windows, 5.5 m for portions with primary windows, and 7.5 m for portions beyond a building length of 25.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: Wall-portion-specific arms cannot be selected from lot data; the 25.0 m threshold is not expressed. Text reads 'main wall with that do not have' (source typo).

units.disclosure: Apartment side setbacks on through lots vary by wall portion; only partly evaluated.

10.10.40.70(1).explanation: Where front-yard averaging does not apply, the front of the building must be at least 6.0 metres from the front lot line.

10.10.40.70(2).explanation: The building must be at least 7.5 metres from the rear lot line.

10.10.40.70(3).explanation: Side yards must be at least 0.9 metres for houses, houseplexes, street-fronting townhouses and apartment buildings up to 13.0 m tall, and 7.5 metres for other townhouses, taller apartment buildings and non-residential buildings.

10.10.40.70(4).explanation: For houses, houseplexes, street-fronting townhouses and low apartment buildings, a side yard can be reduced to 0.45 metres on a side of the building with no windows or doors.

10.10.40.70(5).explanation: Townhouses and apartment buildings on a major street have their own setbacks: front 3.0 to 6.0 m depending on lot depth, rear 7.5 m, and side yards from 0.9 to 7.5 m depending on unit orientation, windows, wall length, corner and through lots.
